lines.text: Your future self is a stranger you keep making promises for.
In one study, office workers picked a snack they'd get a week later.
But when the snack was for right now, most grabbed chocolate.
Psychologists call it present bias. Now always feels bigger than later.
So here's the trick. Make the good choice in advance, before temptation is in the room.
Your future self will thank you. Follow for one new trick your brain plays on you, every day.

post.title: Why You Always Choose Now Over Later #shorts
post.description: Present bias: in Read & van Leeuwen's 1998 study, office workers choosing a snack for next week mostly picked fruit, but for right now most picked chocolate. Decide in advance. #psychology #shorts #selfcontrol #habits
